angle: token geometry of the quantizer input: fixed versus learned front end at matched reconstruction
study_sentence: A seed-paired training experiment in which the front end of one EEG tokenizer is assigned to a learned convolution, a frozen filter bank, the frozen filter bank with a fixed whitening, with rank-matched noise or with centring only, with the codebook perplexity of held-out code assignments at steps 10,000-16,000 as the outcome, on sleep EEG (ISRUC, Sleep-EDF) and repeated descriptively on awake EEG (EEGBCI).
question: Can the codebook perplexity deficit of a frozen filter-bank front end against a learned convolution in an EEG tokenizer be at least halved without training the front end by a fixed whitening of its tokens, and does whitening gain more than rank-matched noise does?

original_question.text: Why does a frozen filter-bank front end that reconstructs as well as a learned convolution give lower codebook perplexity in an EEG tokenizer: is the deficit set by the anisotropy of its tokens, which a fixed whitening removes without any training, or by the absence of a trained front end?
original_question.changed_because: restatement: the blind reader found that only the whitening part carries a pass/fail rule and that no arm trains the filter bank, so the either/or about a trained front end and the causal 'set by anisotropy' wording were removed; the question now asks what the experiments test; after restatement 2 'be removed' became 'be at least halved', which is what the rule tests

angle_parts.part: token geometry of the quantizer input

datasets: ISRUC-Sleep + Sleep-EDF telemetry (project h5, one preprocessing pipeline)
inventory: ~/mne_data/MNE-eegbci-data: 109 subjects, awake, other amplifier, no ASR needed - used as the second dataset in E6
~/mne_data/sleep-edf-s3: 20 raw Sleep-EDF cassette recordings, 2 EEG channels - would serve as a third pool, not used to keep the budget

claims.statement: Although the codebook perplexity deficit of a frozen filter-bank front end against a learned convolution is read as the price of not training it, a fixed whitening of its tokens closes at least half of that deficit and more of it than rank-matched noise does, which we conjecture is because the encoder cannot use signal directions that are small beside the tokens' dominant modes.
reasons: A fixed map on the frozen front end's tokens, with no gradient reaching the front end, raises codebook perplexity by at least half of the gap to the learned convolution at unchanged validation reconstruction.
Noise that raises the tokens' rank to the same value gains less, by at least a quarter of the deficit.

evidence.measure: codes assigned to 20,000 held-out validation patches at steps 10,000, 12,000, 14,000, 16,000 -> perplexity = exp(entropy of the code histogram) per evaluation point -> mean of the four per run -> per seed G = P_W - P_F and D = P_L - P_F -> mean and one-sided 95% bounds of G - 0.5 D over 5 seeds; validation loss averaged over the same four points and the seeds; the same statistic at step 16,000 alone; code informativeness per run
evidence.would_show: the lower bound of mean(G - 0.5 D) above 0 with W's validation loss inside the guard
evidence.refuted_if: the upper one-sided 95% bound of mean(G - 0.5 D) is below 0 on the four-point mean and at step 16,000 alone, or W's validation loss (mean of the evaluation points and the seeds) exceeds F's by more than the larger of 1% and twice the between-seed SD of F's, or W's code informativeness (share of held-out Fourier-amplitude target variance explained by the assigned code's mean target) is below F's by more than twice its between-seed SD
evidence.can_fail: yes: the map acts on the 256-dimensional token at the encoder's input and the measure is the code histogram after 12 trained layers; the encoder may give raw and whitened tokens the same z distribution, or whitening may lower usage

evidence.measure: codes assigned to 20,000 held-out validation patches at steps 10,000, 12,000, 14,000, 16,000 -> perplexity = exp(entropy of the code histogram) per evaluation point -> mean of the four per run -> per seed H = P_W - P_N for arm N (frozen bank + rank-matched noise) -> per seed H - 0.25 D -> mean and one-sided 95% bounds over 5 seeds; code informativeness of N beside W
evidence.would_show: the lower bound of mean(H - 0.25 D) above 0
evidence.refuted_if: the upper one-sided 95% bound of mean(H - 0.25 D) is below 0 (supported on this experiment if the lower bound is above 0, otherwise undecided)
evidence.can_fail: yes: the noise is added to the same tokens the encoder reads and reaches the same rank, so it can gain as much as whitening

evidence.measure: the E2 path on EEGBCI (6 channels, 250 Hz), arms L, F, W, 2 seeds, evaluation at steps 8,000, 10,000, 12,000: mean G and mean D
evidence.would_show: the same sign and a closure of at least half
evidence.refuted_if: none stated as a test: with 2 seeds mean G against 0.5 x mean D is reported as agreement or disagreement in sign and size
evidence.can_fail: yes: as E2, on data with another spectrum and a single corpus

construction.predictor_formula: t'_i = s * C_shrunk^(-1/2) * (t_i - m), C_shrunk = 0.9*C + 0.1*(tr C / 256)*I, m and C from 20,000 training patches
construction.outcome_formula: P = exp(-sum_k q_k * ln q_k) averaged over four evaluation points, q_k = share of 20,000 held-out patches assigned to code k; statistics G - 0.5*D and H
construction.computable_without_experiment: no: q_k depends on the encoder and codebook trained for 16,000 steps under each arm, which no existing data give (that whitened tokens have a higher rank is algebra and that noise matches it is by construction; neither is in the rule)
construction.free_quantity: how the jointly trained encoder and the EMA cosine codebook transmit the geometry of their input to held-out code usage

claims.warrant: When a fixed map on a frozen front end's output, with the front end untrained in both arms, changes an outcome of the trained model, then that change is obtainable without training the front end.

outcomes.if_supported: we learn that a fixed normalisation stage, without gradients in the front end, at least halves the deficit in code usage and does so beyond what added rank explains
outcomes.if_not: we learn that flattening the token spectrum does not remove the deficit, or does no more than noise, so what a trained front end supplies must be sought elsewhere

negation.text: A fixed whitening closes less than half of the deficit, or no more of it than rank-matched noise.

expected_direction.direction: whitening raises held-out codebook perplexity, and by more than rank-matched noise
expected_direction.basis: contested: zhaoetal2026 predicts a gain from flattening what is quantized; the project record's reading and andersonetal2023 (a non-moving front end is an optimisation failure) predict that training is what is missing

claims.falsifier: E2: the upper one-sided 95% bound of mean(G - 0.5 D) over 5 seeds is below 0 on the four-point mean and at step 16,000 alone, or W's validation loss (mean of the evaluation points and the seeds) exceeds F's by more than the larger of 1% and twice the between-seed SD of F's, or W's code informativeness (share of held-out Fourier-amplitude target variance explained by the assigned code's mean target) is below F's by more than twice its between-seed SD (supported if the lower bound is above 0 on both readings and the guards hold; undecided otherwise, including when the two readings disagree); read only if E1 shows mean D > 0 at one-sided paired p < 0.05. E4 has its own three-way rule on mean(H - 0.25 D).

rivals.how: whitening amplifies low-variance token directions that carry noise, so codes spread over noise and perplexity rises without the encoder gaining usable signal
perplexity varies between runs and only 5 seeds are used
rivals.ruled_out_by: E2 (one-sided 95% bounds over paired seeds, three-way outcome)

rivals.how: the evaluation points, the guard or the thresholds could be chosen after seeing the curves
rivals.ruled_out_by: design: evaluation points, guard and thresholds fixed before any run

rivals.how: whitening changes the token scale and so the effective step size of the encoder
rivals.ruled_out_by: design: the scalar s matches the mean squared token norm of W to F; arm C (E5) separates mean removal

rivals.how: whitening statistics or the outcome computed on data the model was fit to
rivals.ruled_out_by: design: m and C from training patches only; perplexity from held-out patches

rivals.how: the bank configuration (48 poles, 8 oscillators) is the most anisotropic one in the project record, so the effect may not hold for other banks

controls.negative: E4: frozen bank + rank-matched noise, 5 seeds; expected under the claim: the lower bound of mean(H - 0.25 D) above 0 and N's code informativeness below W's; under the main rival H is about 0
controls.negative_can_move: yes: the noise is added to the tokens the encoder reads, where whitening acts
controls.positive: E1: the learned convolution against the frozen bank, the contrast the project record reports
controls.positive_expected: D = P_L - P_F is a signed difference of means with no absolute value, rank or clip, so a known difference comes back unchanged: +109 on EMA usage in the project record (397 vs 288, one seed, 15 patches); with held-out assignments at 4 patches the size is unknown and the sign is expected positive

scope.internal: for this tokenizer, bank configuration and training length, whether a fixed whitening removes at least half of the deficit and beats rank-matched noise
scope.external: suggests fixed front ends need a normalisation stage in VQ tokenizers; does not generalise to other bank configurations, longer training, downstream accuracy or other quantizers
limits: one bank configuration (48 poles, 8 oscillators, 4 bins)
16,000 steps with 4 patches per window, not the 44,000 steps and 15 patches of the project record
the conjectured reason (signal directions small beside the dominant modes) is not tested beyond the noise control
code usage only: no masked pretraining or fine-tuning
'at least halved', not removed; the thresholds 0.5 and 0.25 are design choices
rank-matched noise also lowers the tokens' signal-to-noise ratio, so E4 separates 'rank alone' from whitening but not every other difference between the two arms

power.min_detectable: d >= 1.11 at 80% power, one-sided alpha = 0.05 (paired, normal approximation)

claims.statement: The deficit in codebook perplexity of the frozen filter-bank front end against the learned convolution, D = P_L - P_F, is estimated over 5 seeds at this scale with its 95% confidence interval.
reasons: The project record has one seed per arm.

evidence.measure: P per run as in E2 -> per seed D = P_L - P_F -> mean and 95% CI over 5 seeds
evidence.would_show: the size and spread of the deficit

claims.warrant: When the same contrast is run from several seeds, then the mean difference and its interval describe the contrast better than one run.

outcomes.if_supported: a deficit with an interval that excludes zero makes the project's single-seed observation a replicated fact
outcomes.if_not: an interval that includes zero says the deficit is within seed noise at this scale

claims.estimate_because: size-open: the direction is the project record's single-seed observation (397 vs 288); its size and seed-to-seed spread at this scale are unknown
claims.precision_target: 95% CI of total width 1.75 SD of the per-seed difference with n = 5 (SD unknown); aim: an interval that separates the deficit from zero

claims.statement: For the five front-end arms the token statistics (effective rank, signal-subspace rank, mean pairwise cosine), the effective rank of the quantizer input and the share of the whitening gain reached by centring alone are reported beside each arm's codebook perplexity.
reasons: The project record found that no offline token statistic predicted the deficit.

evidence.measure: token statistics on 8,800 held-out patches per arm; effective rank of z at step 16,000 per run -> mean per arm; listed with mean perplexity
evidence.would_show: which statistic orders the arms as perplexity does

evidence.measure: arm C (frozen bank, mean token removed), 3 seeds: (P_C - P_F) / (P_W - P_F) per seed
evidence.would_show: the share of the whitening gain that centring alone reaches

claims.warrant: When several candidate statistics are listed beside an outcome over the same arms, then the ones that order the arms differently from the outcome are poor predictors of it.

outcomes.if_supported: a statistic that orders the arms as perplexity does becomes a candidate offline screen for front ends
outcomes.if_not: no offline statistic orders them, as the project record found, and the screen has to be a training run

claims.estimate_because: descriptive: five arms give an ordering and one ratio at n = 3, not a test
claims.precision_target: per-arm means over 5 (L, F, W, N) or 3 (C) seeds with their ranges; no interval aimed for

sample.target: EEG tokenizers trained on multi-corpus EEG
sample.accessible: one tokenizer architecture on 55 h of sleep EEG, 5 seeds, plus EEGBCI
sample.concern: small corpus and short training; the project's preprocessing left quality defects in the sleep pool

predictor.phenomenon: the second-order geometry of what the front end hands to the encoder
predictor.validity: construct: whitening changes only mean and covariance of the tokens (manipulation check E0)

outcome.phenomenon: how much of the codebook the tokenizer uses
outcome.precision: between-seed spread unknown; estimated in E1
outcome.accuracy: exact for the EMA usage the quantizer keeps
outcome.validity: content: the usage entropy the VQ literature reports (fangetal2025, takida2022); it is not a measure of downstream usefulness

tradeoffs.change: the primary claim no longer asserts that the deficit is set by the tokens' anisotropy; it asserts that a fixed whitening is sufficient to remove at least half of it and beats rank-matched noise, with the reason stated as a conjecture
tradeoffs.because: the reader showed that the experiments can establish sufficiency of an intervention, not the cause of the deficit, and that no arm trains the bank
tradeoffs.lost: the causal attribution of the deficit to anisotropy, and the contrast with a trained front end
tradeoffs.why: the question was rewritten to the tested part (original_question); the gap (front end varied at matched reconstruction with the codebook as outcome, and whether token variance structure rather than learning sets it) is still addressed by the sufficiency test; the angle's three phrases keep their experiments

tradeoffs.change: E6 (second dataset, 2 seeds) changed role from tests to descriptive
tradeoffs.because: the second reader pointed out that an experiment labelled as a test carried no test
tradeoffs.lost: nothing: it never had the seeds to test; the label now says so
tradeoffs.why: the tested contrast is E2 and E4 on the primary pool

tradeoffs.change: other bank configurations (12 poles, 26 oscillators) were not included
tradeoffs.because: budget: each configuration needs its own F and W runs
tradeoffs.lost: whether the result holds for less anisotropic banks
tradeoffs.why: the question is asked of the configuration whose deficit is documented; the limit is in scope

reader_doubts.doubt: 1. Passing E2 shows an intervention is sufficient, not that anisotropy caused the deficit; no arm trains the bank; whitening changes centring, variance and scale at once
reader_doubts.how: C1 restated as a sufficiency claim with the reason marked as a conjecture; the question narrowed (original_question); arm C (centring only) added as E5

reader_doubts.doubt: 2. The noise control is matched on effective rank, which was the proposal's own anisotropy measure; E4 had 3 seeds and no test
reader_doubts.how: anisotropy removed from C1; the claim now says whitening must beat rank-matched noise; E4 has 5 seeds and its own refuted_if in C1's evidence

reader_doubts.doubt: 3. The rule compared point estimates of two noisy means and did not say what decides
reader_doubts.how: E2 and C1's falsifier now use one-sided 95% bounds with a three-way outcome (supported / refuted / undecided)

reader_doubts.doubt: 4a. Perplexity was read from EMA usage counts, not held-out assignments
reader_doubts.how: E1, E2, E4 and E5 read perplexity from codes assigned to 20,000 held-out patches at four evaluation points

reader_doubts.doubt: 4b. The deficit may not exist at 16,000 steps and 4 patches; the project record is 44,000 steps and 15 patches
reader_doubts.how: budget: 23 runs at 44,000 steps and 15 patches cost about 65 CPU-hours at the timed 0.23 s per step; E1 stays a precondition and non-replication is reported

reader_doubts.doubt: 5. The reconstruction guard allowed 5% at a single step with no aggregation rule
reader_doubts.how: E2's guard is the larger of 1% and twice the between-seed SD of F's validation loss, averaged over four evaluation points and the seeds

reader_doubts.doubt: 6. One tokenizer and the most anisotropic bank configuration; the awake repeat has 2 seeds and no test
reader_doubts.how: budget: a second bank configuration needs 10 more runs (about 7 CPU-hours) and E6 at 5 seeds 9 more (about 6 CPU-hours) on top of about 19; the draft no longer presents E6 as confirmation

reader_doubts.doubt: 7. Perplexity is not downstream usefulness; no masked pretraining or fine-tuning
reader_doubts.how: budget: stage-2 pretraining and fine-tuning for 5 arms and 5 seeds is several hours per run on this CPU; the claim is limited to code usage in scope and title

reader_doubts.doubt: 8. Decision rules are not externally timestamped
reader_doubts.how: E0 states that the plan with all rules is committed (hash recorded) before the first training run; the risk entry remains for the case that it is not

reader_doubts.doubt: Minor: experiment ids skip E5
reader_doubts.how: E5 is now the centring-only arm

reader_doubts.doubt: 1. The deficit may not be present at this scale and on held-out perplexity; half of a small D is an unstable target
reader_doubts.how: budget: 23 runs at the project's 44,000 steps and 15 patches cost about 65 CPU-hours; E1 remains a precondition

reader_doubts.doubt: 2. Five paired seeds detect only d >= 1.11; the E1 gate is a p < 0.05 test at n = 5
reader_doubts.how: budget: 10 seeds for the four tested arms add 20 runs (about 13 CPU-hours) to about 19; the three-way rule reports undecided instead of forcing a verdict

reader_doubts.doubt: 3. E4 had only a refutation rule and used mean D as a fixed number
reader_doubts.how: E4 now reads per-seed H - 0.25 D with a three-way rule (supported / refuted / undecided)

reader_doubts.doubt: 4. Isotropic noise changes signal-to-noise as well as rank; whitening may spend codes on amplified noise; the validation-loss guard is weak
reader_doubts.how: E2 and E4 add code informativeness (held-out target variance explained by the assigned code) as a guard and as a reported contrast between W and N; the remaining confound is listed in C1's scope limits

reader_doubts.doubt: 5. A difference in the 10,000-16,000 mean could be a difference in filling speed
reader_doubts.how: E2's rule is read on the four-point mean and at step 16,000 alone; disagreement gives undecided; the slope between the two is reported

reader_doubts.doubt: 6. One tokenizer, one quantizer, the most anisotropic bank, one data pool; the second dataset untested
reader_doubts.how: budget: a second bank configuration needs 10 more runs (about 7 CPU-hours) and E6 at 5 seeds 9 more (about 6 CPU-hours)

reader_doubts.doubt: 7. 'Removed' and 'enough' outrun a half-closure rule
reader_doubts.how: question, title and abstract now say 'at least halved'

reader_doubts.doubt: 8. The explanation is untested; a success shows that whitening helps, not why
reader_doubts.how: budget: testing the conjecture needs arms that rescale selected directions only (at least 2 more arms x 5 seeds, about 7 CPU-hours); it is stated as a conjecture and a scope limit

reader_doubts.doubt: 9. Not externally timestamped
reader_doubts.how: E0 requires the committed plan hash before the first run; the risk entry stays for the case it is skipped

reader_doubts.doubt: 10. E6 tagged as a test without one; E1 descriptive but gating; 'the whole question is tested'
reader_doubts.how: E6's role is descriptive; E1's entry states its precondition; with E4's three-way rule both parts of the question carry a rule
